sections.title: Example 1: Grid Search Cross-Validation
sections.body:
```python
print("\nExample 1: Grid Search Cross-Validation")
print("-" * 50)

# Generate classification data
X_clf, y_clf = make_classification(
    n_samples=1000,
    n_features=10,
    n_informative=8,
    n_redundant=2,
    n_classes=2,
    random_state=42,
)
X_train_clf, X_test_clf, y_train_clf, y_test_clf = train_test_split(
    X_clf, y_clf, test_size=0.2, random_state=42, stratify=y_clf
)

# Define parameter grid for Random Forest
param_grid_rf = {
    "n_estimators": [50, 100, 200],
    "max_depth": [None, 5, 10, 15],
    "min_samples_split": [2, 5, 10],
    "min_samples_leaf": [1, 2, 4],
    "max_features": ["sqrt", "log2", None],
}

# Perform Grid Search
rf = RandomForestClassifier(random_state=42)
grid_search = GridSearchCV(
    rf, param_grid_rf, cv=5, scoring="accuracy", n_jobs=-1, verbose=1
)
grid_search.fit(X_train_clf, y_train_clf)

# Results
print(f"Best parameters: {grid_search.best_params_}")
print(f"Best cross-validation score: {grid_search.best_score_:.4f}")
print(f"Test set score: {grid_search.score(X_test_clf, y_test_clf):.4f}")

# Visualize results
results_df = pd.DataFrame(grid_search.cv_results_)
results_df = results_df.sort_values("rank_test_score")

# Plot top 10 results
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
top_10 = results_df.head(10)
plt.barh(range(len(top_10)), top_10["mean_test_score"])
plt.yticks(range(len(top_10)), [f"Config {i+1}" for i in range(len(top_10))])
plt.xlabel("Cross-validation Score")
plt.title("Top 10 Grid Search Configurations")
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()
```

sections.title: Example 3: Bayesian Optimization with Optuna
sections.body:
```python
print("\nExample 3: Bayesian Optimization with Optuna")
print("-" * 50)

try:
    import optuna

    # Define objective function for Optuna
    def objective(trial):
        # Define hyperparameters
        n_estimators = trial.suggest_int("n_estimators", 50, 300)
        max_depth = trial.suggest_int("max_depth", 3, 20)
        min_samples_split = trial.suggest_int("min_samples_split", 2, 20)
        min_samples_leaf = trial.suggest_int("min_samples_leaf", 1, 10)
        max_features = trial.suggest_categorical("max_features", ["sqrt", "log2", None])

        # Create model
        model = RandomForestClassifier(
            n_estimators=n_estimators,
            max_depth=max_depth,
            min_samples_split=min_samples_split,
            min_samples_leaf=min_samples_leaf,
            max_features=max_features,
            random_state=42,
        )

        # Evaluate using cross-validation
        scores = cross_val_score(
            model, X_train_clf, y_train_clf, cv=5, scoring="accuracy"
        )
        return scores.mean()

    # Create study and optimize
    study = optuna.create_study(direction="maximize")
    study.optimize(objective, n_trials=50)

    # Results
    print(f"Best trial: {study.best_trial.value:.4f}")
    print(f"Best parameters: {study.best_trial.params}")

    # Train best model
    best_model = RandomForestClassifier(**study.best_trial.params, random_state=42)
    best_model.fit(X_train_clf, y_train_clf)
    test_score = best_model.score(X_test_clf, y_test_clf)
    print(f"Test set score: {test_score:.4f}")

    # Plot optimization history
    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 5))

    plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
    optuna.visualization.matplotlib.plot_optimization_history(study)
    plt.title("Optimization History")

    plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
    optuna.visualization.matplotlib.plot_param_importances(study)
    plt.title("Parameter Importances")

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

except ImportError:
    print("Optuna not installed. Install with: pip install optuna")
    print("Skipping Bayesian optimization example.")
```

sections.title: Example 4: Manual Hyperparameter Tuning
sections.body:
```python
print("\nExample 4: Manual Hyperparameter Tuning")
print("-" * 50)

# Generate regression data
X_reg, y_reg = make_regression(n_samples=1000, n_features=5, noise=20, random_state=42)
X_train_reg, X_test_reg, y_train_reg, y_test_reg = train_test_split(
    X_reg, y_reg, test_size=0.2, random_state=42
)

# Manual tuning for Ridge Regression
alpha_values = [0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000]
cv_scores = []
test_scores = []

for alpha in alpha_values:
    # Cross-validation
    ridge = Ridge(alpha=alpha)
    cv_score = cross_val_score(
        ridge, X_train_reg, y_train_reg, cv=5, scoring="r2"
    ).mean()
    cv_scores.append(cv_score)

    # Test set evaluation
    ridge.fit(X_train_reg, y_train_reg)
    test_score = ridge.score(X_test_reg, y_test_reg)
    test_scores.append(test_score)

    print(f"Alpha: {alpha:>7}, CV Score: {cv_score:.4f}, Test Score: {test_score:.4f}")

# Find best alpha
best_alpha_idx = np.argmax(cv_scores)
best_alpha = alpha_values[best_alpha_idx]
print(f"\nBest alpha: {best_alpha}")
print(f"Best CV score: {cv_scores[best_alpha_idx]:.4f}")
print(f"Corresponding test score: {test_scores[best_alpha_idx]:.4f}")

# Plot learning curves
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 5))

plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
plt.semilogx(alpha_values, cv_scores, "bo-", label="CV Score")
plt.semilogx(alpha_values, test_scores, "ro-", label="Test Score")
plt.axvline(
    x=best_alpha, color="green", linestyle="--", label=f"Best Alpha: {best_alpha}"
)
plt.xlabel("Alpha (Regularization Strength)")
plt.ylabel("R² Score")
plt.title("Ridge Regression - Alpha Tuning")
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Learning curves for different alphas
plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
train_sizes = np.linspace(0.1, 1.0, 10)
selected_alphas = [0.01, 1, 100]

for alpha in selected_alphas:
    train_scores = []
    for size in train_sizes:
        n_samples = int(size * len(X_train_reg))
        ridge = Ridge(alpha=alpha)
        score = cross_val_score(
            ridge, X_train_reg[:n_samples], y_train_reg[:n_samples], cv=3, scoring="r2"
        ).mean()
        train_scores.append(score)

    plt.plot(train_sizes, train_scores, "o-", label=f"Alpha = {alpha}")

plt.xlabel("Training Set Size (fraction)")
plt.ylabel("R² Score")
plt.title("Learning Curves for Different Alphas")
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

sections.body:
```python
print("\nExample 5: Hyperparameter Tuning for Multiple Algorithms")
print("-" * 50)

# Define parameter grids for different algorithms
param_grids = {
    "Random Forest": {
        "n_estimators": [50, 100, 200],
        "max_depth": [None, 10, 20],
        "min_samples_split": [2, 5, 10],
    },
    "Logistic Regression": {
        "C": [0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100],
        "penalty": ["l1", "l2"],
        "solver": ["liblinear", "saga"],
    },
    "SVM": {
        "C": [0.1, 1, 10, 100],
        "kernel": ["rbf", "linear"],
        "gamma": ["scale", "auto", 0.001, 0.01, 0.1],
    },
}

models = {
    "Random Forest": RandomForestClassifier(random_state=42),
    "Logistic Regression": LogisticRegression(random_state=42, max_iter=1000),
    "SVM": SVC(random_state=42, probability=True),
}

# Compare all algorithms
results = {}

for name, model in models.items():
    print(f"\nTuning {name}...")

    # Grid search
    grid_search = GridSearchCV(
        model, param_grids[name], cv=5, scoring="accuracy", n_jobs=-1
    )
    grid_search.fit(X_train_clf, y_train_clf)

    # Store results
    results[name] = {
        "best_params": grid_search.best_params_,
        "cv_score": grid_search.best_score_,
        "test_score": grid_search.score(X_test_clf, y_test_clf),
    }

    print(f"Best parameters: {grid_search.best_params_}")
    print(f"CV Score: {grid_search.best_score_:.4f}")
    print(f"Test Score: {grid_search.score(X_test_clf, y_test_clf):.4f}")

# Visualize comparison
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(15, 6))

# CV Scores comparison
cv_scores = [results[name]["cv_score"] for name in results.keys()]
test_scores = [results[name]["test_score"] for name in results.keys()]

x = np.arange(len(results))
width = 0.35

axes[0].bar(x - width / 2, cv_scores, width, label="CV Score", alpha=0.8)
axes[0].bar(x + width / 2, test_scores, width, label="Test Score", alpha=0.8)
axes[0].set_xlabel("Algorithm")
axes[0].set_ylabel("Accuracy Score")
axes[0].set_title("Algorithm Comparison")
axes[0].set_xticks(x)
axes[0].set_xticklabels(results.keys(), rotation=45)
axes[0].legend()
axes[0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Best algorithm
best_algorithm = max(results.keys(), key=lambda x: results[x]["cv_score"])
axes[1].text(
    0.5,
    0.5,
    f'Best Algorithm:\n{best_algorithm}\n\nCV Score: {results[best_algorithm]["cv_score"]:.4f}\nTest Score: {results[best_algorithm]["test_score"]:.4f}',
    ha="center",
    va="center",
    fontsize=14,
    bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", facecolor="lightblue"),
)
axes[1].set_xlim(0, 1)
axes[1].set_ylim(0, 1)
axes[1].set_title("Best Algorithm Summary")
axes[1].axis("off")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

sections.title: Example 6: Advanced Bayesian Optimization with Hyperopt
sections.body:
```python
print("\nExample 6: Advanced Bayesian Optimization with Hyperopt")
print("-" * 50)

try:
    from hyperopt import fmin, tpe, hp, STATUS_OK, Trials

    # Define search space
    space = {
        "n_estimators": hp.choice("n_estimators", [50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300]),
        "max_depth": hp.choice("max_depth", [None, 3, 5, 7, 10, 15, 20]),
        "min_samples_split": hp.choice("min_samples_split", [2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 15]),
        "min_samples_leaf": hp.choice("min_samples_leaf", [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]),
        "max_features": hp.choice("max_features", ["sqrt", "log2", None]),
        "bootstrap": hp.choice("bootstrap", [True, False]),
    }

    # Define objective function
    def objective(params):
        model = RandomForestClassifier(**params, random_state=42)
        score = cross_val_score(
            model, X_train_clf, y_train_clf, cv=5, scoring="accuracy"
        ).mean()
        return {"loss": -score, "status": STATUS_OK}

    # Run optimization
    trials = Trials()
    best = fmin(
        fn=objective, space=space, algo=tpe.suggest, max_evals=50, trials=trials
    )

    print(f"Best parameters: {best}")
    print(f"Best CV score: {-trials.best_trial['result']['loss']:.4f}")

    # Train best model
    best_model = RandomForestClassifier(**best, random_state=42)
    best_model.fit(X_train_clf, y_train_clf)
    test_score = best_model.score(X_test_clf, y_test_clf)
    print(f"Test set score: {test_score:.4f}")

    # Plot optimization progress
    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 5))

    # Loss over trials
    losses = [trial["result"]["loss"] for trial in trials.trials]
    plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
    plt.plot(losses)
    plt.xlabel("Trial")
    plt.ylabel("Loss (-CV Score)")
    plt.title("Hyperopt Optimization Progress")
    plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

    # Best loss over trials
    best_losses = []
    current_best = float("inf")
    for loss in losses:
        if loss < current_best:
            current_best = loss
        best_losses.append(current_best)

    plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
    plt.plot(best_losses)
    plt.xlabel("Trial")
    plt.ylabel("Best Loss (-CV Score)")
    plt.title("Best Loss Over Trials")
    plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

except ImportError:
    print("Hyperopt not installed. Install with: pip install hyperopt")
    print("Skipping Hyperopt example.")
```

sections.title: Example 7: Nested Cross-Validation for Unbiased Estimates
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Exercise 1: Grid Search vs Random Search Comparison Compare grid search and random search on the same dataset with the same computational budget.
- Project 1: Automated Hyperparameter Tuning System Process: 1.
- Hyperparameter tuning is crucial for optimal model performance 2.
- Outer CV for unbiased estimate
- Split data for this fold
- Inner CV for hyperparameter tuning
- Evaluate on outer test set
- Compare with regular CV

```python
print("\nExample 7: Nested Cross-Validation for Unbiased Estimates")

from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score

# Outer CV for unbiased estimate
outer_cv_scores = []
best_models = []

# Outer CV loop
for i in range(5):
    # Split data for this fold
    X_outer_train, X_outer_test, y_outer_train, y_outer_test = train_test_split(
        X_clf, y_clf, test_size=0.2, random_state=i, stratify=y_clf
    )

    # Inner CV for hyperparameter tuning
    inner_grid_search = GridSearchCV(
        RandomForestClassifier(random_state=42),
        param_grid_rf,
        cv=3,
        scoring="accuracy",
        n_jobs=-1,
    )
    inner_grid_search.fit(X_outer_train, y_outer_train)

    # Evaluate on outer test set
    outer_score = inner_grid_search.score(X_outer_test, y_outer_test)
    outer_cv_scores.append(outer_score)
    best_models.append(inner_grid_search.best_estimator_)

    print(
        f"Fold {i+1}: CV Score = {inner_grid_search.best_score_:.4f}, Test Score = {outer_score:.4f}"
    )

print(f"\nNested CV Results:")
print(
    f"Mean CV Score: {np.mean(outer_cv_scores):.4f} (+/- {np.std(outer_cv_scores) * 2:.4f})"
)

# Compare with regular CV
regular_cv_scores = cross_val_score(
    RandomForestClassifier(random_state=42), X_clf, y_clf, cv=5, scoring="accuracy"
)
print(
    f"Regular CV Score: {regular_cv_scores.mean():.4f} (+/- {regular_cv_scores.std() * 2:.4f})"
)

# Visualize comparison
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.boxplot([outer_cv_scores, regular_cv_scores], labels=["Nested CV", "Regular CV"])
plt.ylabel("Accuracy Score")
plt.title("Nested vs Regular Cross-Validation")
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()
```
